judgment.english: Development. The maiden is given in marriage. Good fortune. Perseverance is favorable. Gradual progress. Each step follows naturally from the last. Nothing is forced or skipped.

lines.chinese: 初六：鴻漸于干，小子厲，有言，無咎。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the shore. The young son is in danger. There is talk. No blame. The first approach — uncertain, exposed, but blameless.

lines.chinese: 六二：鴻漸于磐，飲食衎衎，吉。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the cliff. Eating and drinking in peace and gladness. Good fortune. A secure resting place has been reached.

lines.chinese: 九三：鴻漸于陸，夫征不復，婦孕不育，凶。利禦寇。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the plateau. The husband goes on expedition and does not return. The wife is pregnant but does not give birth. Misfortune. It is favorable to resist marauders. Advance has gone too far from its base.

lines.chinese: 六四：鴻漸于木，或得其桷，無咎。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the tree. Perhaps it finds a flat branch. No blame. An unusual perch, but one manages to find a foothold.

lines.chinese: 九五：鴻漸于陵，婦三歲不孕，終莫之勝，吉。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the summit. For three years the wife has no child. In the end nothing can prevent it. Good fortune. What unfolds naturally cannot ultimately be obstructed.

lines.chinese: 上九：鴻漸于陸，其羽可用為儀，吉。
lines.english: The wild goose gradually draws near the high plateau. Its feathers can be used as ornaments. Good fortune. The journey is complete — what was lived becomes something beautiful and useful.

image.chinese: 澤上有雷，歸妹。君子以永終知敝。
image.english: Thunder over the lake: The Marrying Maiden. The noble one understands the transitory in light of the eternal. Recognize what will wear out. Endure through understanding, not through force.

judgment.chinese: 歸妹：征凶，無攸利。
judgment.english: The Marrying Maiden. Undertakings bring misfortune. Nothing that is favorable. Entering a situation where one holds no real power. The arrangement is fixed; initiative within it will not succeed. One must accept a subordinate position.

lines.chinese: 初九：歸妹以娣，跛能履，征吉。
lines.english: The marrying maiden as a concubine. A lame person who can still walk. Undertakings bring good fortune. Even in a lesser position, one can act and move forward.

lines.chinese: 九二：眇能視，利幽人之貞。
lines.english: A one-eyed person who can still see. The perseverance of a solitary person is favorable. Limited sight, but clear enough. Loyalty in obscurity.

lines.chinese: 六三：歸妹以須，反歸以娣。
lines.english: The marrying maiden as a slave. She goes back and becomes a concubine. What was too low finds a better position — but only by returning and beginning again.

lines.chinese: 九四：歸妹愆期，遲歸有時。
lines.english: The marrying maiden draws out the allotted time. A late marriage comes in due course. The right moment has not yet arrived. Wait.

lines.chinese: 六五：帝乙歸妹，其君之袂不如其娣之袂良。月幾望，吉。
lines.english: Emperor Yi gives his daughter in marriage. The embroidered garments of the princess are not as fine as those of the serving maid. The moon is nearly full. Good fortune. True worth does not depend on display.

lines.chinese: 上六：女承筐無實，士刲羊無血，無攸利。
lines.english: The woman holds the basket, but it is empty. The man sacrifices the sheep, but no blood flows. Nothing is favorable. The forms are maintained but the substance is gone.

image.chinese: 雷電皆至，豐。君子以折獄致刑。
image.english: Thunder and lightning both arrive: Abundance. The noble one decides lawsuits and carries out punishments. In times of fullness, clarity and decisive action are both possible and required.

judgment.chinese: 豐：亨，王假之，勿憂，宜日中。
judgment.english: Abundance. Success. The king attains fullness. Do not be sorrowful. It is fitting to be like the sun at midday. Abundance does not last, but that is no reason to hold back from it. Be present at the peak.

lines.chinese: 初九：遇其配主，雖旬無咎，往有尚。
lines.english: Meeting one's destined ruler. Though they are equals for a full period, there is no blame. Going forward is praiseworthy. A partnership of matched strength at the right moment.

lines.chinese: 六二：豐其蔀，日中見斗，往得疑疾，有孚發若，吉。
lines.english: The curtain is of such fullness that the polestar can be seen at noon. Going forward invites mistrust and illness. If one rouses them through sincerity, good fortune. When abundance obscures, only truthfulness can penetrate.

lines.chinese: 九三：豐其沛，日中見沬，折其右肱，無咎。
lines.english: The underbrush is of such abundance that small stars are seen at noon. One breaks one's right arm. No blame. Darkness at the height of the day — one's capacity is limited. Accept it without forcing.

lines.chinese: 九四：豐其蔀，日中見斗，遇其夷主，吉。
lines.english: The curtain is of such fullness that the polestar can be seen at noon. One meets one's shadow ruler. Good fortune. In the darkness of excess, finding the complementary force brings light.

lines.chinese: 六五：來章，有慶譽，吉。
lines.english: Lines of beauty come. Blessing and fame draw near. Good fortune. By remaining open and receptive at the height of abundance, what is excellent arrives of its own accord.

lines.chinese: 上六：豐其屋，蔀其家，闚其戶，闃其無人，三歲不覿，凶。
lines.english: Abundance in the house — the family is screened off. Peering through the gate, it is still and empty. For three years no one is seen. Misfortune. Abundance that isolates is no abundance at all.

image.chinese: 山上有火，旅。君子以明慎用刑而不留獄。
image.english: Fire on the mountain: The Wanderer. The noble one is clear-minded and cautious in applying punishments, and does not prolong lawsuits. Fire on the mountain burns briefly and moves on. Act with clarity, then release.

judgment.chinese: 旅：小亨，旅貞吉。
judgment.english: The Wanderer. Small success. Perseverance of the wanderer brings good fortune. The traveler cannot expect what the settled person has. Small, careful conduct — not grand ambition — is what serves.

lines.chinese: 初六：旅瑣瑣，斯其所取災。
lines.english: The wanderer busies himself with trivial things. This is how he draws disaster upon himself. Small-mindedness on the road invites misfortune.

lines.chinese: 六二：旅即次，懷其資，得童僕貞。
lines.english: The wanderer arrives at the inn. He carries his property with him. He gains the perseverance of a young servant. Finding shelter, keeping what one has, earning steady loyalty — enough.

lines.chinese: 九三：旅焚其次，喪其童僕，貞厲。
lines.english: The wanderer's inn burns down. He loses his young servant. Perseverance is dangerous. Harshness destroys the shelter one has found and drives away those who serve.

lines.chinese: 九四：旅于處，得其資斧，我心不快。
lines.english: The wanderer rests in a shelter. He obtains his property and an axe. My heart is not glad. One has means and tools but no true home. Security without belonging.

lines.chinese: 六五：射雉一矢亡，終以譽命。
lines.english: Shooting a pheasant — one arrow is lost. In the end one receives praise and appointment. Something is sacrificed in the offering, but what comes back is recognition and purpose.

lines.chinese: 上九：鳥焚其巢，旅人先笑後號啕。喪牛于易，凶。
lines.english: The bird burns its own nest. The wanderer first laughs, then cries and laments. One loses an ox at the border. Misfortune. Carelessness at the end destroys what was built along the way.

image.chinese: 隨風，巽。君子以申命行事。
image.english: Winds following one upon another: The Gentle. The noble one spreads commands abroad and carries out undertakings. Repeated gentle influence — not a single decree but a steady presence that permeates.

judgment.chinese: 巽：小亨，利有攸往，利見大人。
judgment.english: The Gentle. Small success. It is favorable to have a direction to go. It is favorable to see the great person. Penetration through gentleness. Not force but persistence — wind that enters every crack.

lines.chinese: 初六：進退，利武人之貞。
lines.english: Advancing and retreating. The perseverance of a warrior is favorable. Indecision at the start — firmness of purpose must be chosen, or gentleness becomes weakness.

lines.chinese: 九二：巽在牀下，用史巫紛若，吉，無咎。
lines.english: The gentle wind penetrates under the bed. Using priests and diviners in great number. Good fortune. No blame. Going deeply beneath the surface. When hidden influences are at work, seek all available clarity.

lines.chinese: 九三：頻巽，吝。
lines.english: Repeated penetration. Humiliation. Too much yielding, too much deliberation — what should be gentle becomes abject.

lines.chinese: 六四：悔亡，田獲三品。
lines.english: Remorse disappears. In the hunt, three kinds of game are caught. Decisive action arising from patient preparation. The gentleness was not weakness — it was readiness.

lines.chinese: 九五：貞吉，悔亡，無不利。無初有終。先庚三日，後庚三日，吉。
lines.english: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. Nothing unfavorable. No beginning, but an end. Three days before the change, three days after: good fortune. What starts obscurely concludes well, if the timing is honored.

lines.chinese: 上九：巽在牀下，喪其資斧，貞凶。
lines.english: The gentle wind penetrates under the bed. One loses one's property and axe. Perseverance brings misfortune. Submission carried too far — one has given away the means to act.

image.chinese: 麗澤，兌。君子以朋友講習。
image.english: Lakes resting one upon the other: The Joyous. The noble one joins with friends for discussion and practice. Joy that deepens through exchange — learning shared is joy doubled.

judgment.chinese: 兌：亨，利貞。
judgment.english: The Joyous. Success. Perseverance is favorable. True joy — not indulgence but the open expression that comes from inner strength. The lake is open above, firm below.

lines.chinese: 初九：和兌，吉。
lines.english: Contented joyousness. Good fortune. Joy without ulterior motive. Harmony that asks for nothing.

lines.chinese: 九二：孚兌，吉，悔亡。
lines.english: Sincere joyousness. Good fortune. Remorse disappears. Joy grounded in truthfulness — no need for empty pleasures when the real thing is present.

lines.chinese: 六三：來兌，凶。
lines.english: Approaching joyousness. Misfortune. Joy sought from without. When one comes looking for it, it is already not the real thing.

lines.chinese: 九四：商兌未寧，介疾有喜。
lines.english: Joyousness that is weighed and considered is not yet at peace. But by warding off what is unwholesome, there is gladness. Choosing between higher and lower pleasures — the discomfort of discernment leads to real joy.

lines.chinese: 九五：孚于剝，有厲。
lines.english: Trust in what is destructive. There is danger. Even in a time of joy, one must recognize what erodes. Sincerity directed toward what strips away brings peril.

lines.chinese: 上六：引兌。
lines.english: Seductive joyousness. Joy that lures, that draws others in. No judgment is given — the outcome depends entirely on what one is being drawn toward.

image.chinese: 風行水上，渙。先王以享于帝立廟。
image.english: Wind blowing over water: Dispersion. The ancient kings made offerings to the Lord on High and built temples. In times of dissolution, the sacred gathering point holds things together. What unites must be higher than what divides.

judgment.chinese: 渙：亨。王假有廟，利涉大川，利貞。
judgment.english: Dispersion. Success. The king approaches his ancestral temple. It is favorable to cross the great water. Perseverance is favorable. What has hardened must be dissolved. The wind over the water scatters what has frozen — rigidity gives way to flow.

lines.chinese: 初六：用拯馬壯，吉。
lines.english: Rescue is carried out with the strength of a horse. Good fortune. Act swiftly at the first sign of dissolution. Early intervention with vigor succeeds.

lines.chinese: 九二：渙奔其機，悔亡。
lines.english: At the dissolution, one runs to one's support. Remorse disappears. When things scatter, go to what is solid. Find the foundation beneath the dispersion.

lines.chinese: 六三：渙其躬，無悔。
lines.english: Dissolving the self. No remorse. Letting go of personal concerns so that the larger work can proceed. Self-forgetting in service of what matters.

lines.chinese: 六四：渙其群，元吉。渙有丘，匪夷所思。
lines.english: Dissolving the group. Supreme good fortune. Dissolution leads to accumulation — what scatters from the smaller gathers into the larger. Something beyond ordinary thinking.

lines.chinese: 九五：渙汗其大號，渙王居，無咎。
lines.english: Dissolution — sweat pours during the great proclamation. Dissolution of the king's stores. No blame. In crisis, the leader gives freely of what has been held. The reserves exist for this moment.

lines.chinese: 上九：渙其血，去逖出，無咎。
lines.english: Dissolving one's blood — departing, keeping at a distance, going out. No blame. Withdrawing from what is harmful. Dissolution here means escape from danger.

image.chinese: 澤上有水，節。君子以制數度，議德行。
image.english: Water over the lake: Limitation. The noble one creates number and measure, and deliberates upon virtue and conduct. Limits must be considered, calibrated — not imposed arbitrarily.

judgment.chinese: 節：亨。苦節不可貞。
judgment.english: Limitation. Success. But bitter limitation must not be persevered in. Limits give shape — the lake can hold water because it has banks. But limitation that is harsh and joyless defeats its own purpose.

lines.chinese: 初九：不出戶庭，無咎。
lines.english: Not going out of the door and courtyard. No blame. Knowing when to stay within bounds. The beginning is a time for restraint, not exploration.

lines.chinese: 九二：不出門庭，凶。
lines.english: Not going out of the gate and courtyard. Misfortune. The same restraint that was right at first becomes wrong when the moment calls for action. Missing the time is the real failure.

lines.chinese: 六三：不節若，則嗟若，無咎。
lines.english: If one does not limit oneself, one will have cause to lament. No blame. Recognizing excess after the fact — the regret itself becomes the teacher.

lines.chinese: 六四：安節，亨。
lines.english: Contented limitation. Success. Limits that are accepted naturally, without strain. The shape fits what it contains.

lines.chinese: 九五：甘節，吉，往有尚。
lines.english: Sweet limitation. Good fortune. Going forward is praiseworthy. Limitation applied to oneself first, and generously. This kind of measure earns trust and opens the way.

lines.chinese: 上六：苦節，貞凶，悔亡。
lines.english: Bitter limitation. Perseverance brings misfortune. Remorse disappears. Severity taken too far. Even though remorse fades — because one was sincere — the harshness still does harm.

image.chinese: 澤上有風，中孚。君子以議獄緩死。
image.english: Wind over the lake: Inner Truth. The noble one deliberates over criminal cases and delays executions. When inner truth guides judgment, one pauses before the irreversible. Sincerity requires patience.

judgment.chinese: 中孚：豚魚吉，利涉大川，利貞。
judgment.english: Inner Truth. Even pigs and fish are moved. Good fortune. It is favorable to cross the great water. Perseverance is favorable. Sincerity so deep it reaches even the most insensible. The inner being is empty and receptive — truth resonates from the center outward.

lines.chinese: 初九：虞吉，有他不燕。
lines.english: Being prepared brings good fortune. If there are secret designs, there is no peace. Inner truth depends on single-mindedness. Divided attention destroys sincerity.

lines.chinese: 九二：鶴鳴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。
lines.english: A crane calling in the shade — its young answers it. I have a fine goblet; I will share it with you. What is genuine calls forth a genuine response. Resonance without contrivance.

lines.chinese: 六三：得敵，或鼓或罷，或泣或歌。
lines.english: Finding a companion — now drumming, now resting, now weeping, now singing. Inner truth has been displaced outward. One's state depends entirely on the other. No center.

lines.chinese: 六四：月幾望，馬匹亡，無咎。
lines.english: The moon is nearly full. The team horse goes astray. No blame. Nearing fullness, one lets go of what paired it to the lower. The ascent toward truth requires leaving something behind.

lines.chinese: 九五：有孚攣如，無咎。
lines.english: Possessing truth that binds together. No blame. Inner truth that holds things in union — not through force but through the gravity of sincerity itself.

lines.chinese: 上九：翰音登于天，貞凶。
lines.english: Cockcrow ascending to heaven. Perseverance brings misfortune. The sound without the substance. When sincerity is only performance — reaching for heaven with a farmyard voice — it cannot hold.

image.chinese: 山上有雷，小過。君子以行過乎恭，喪過乎哀，用過乎儉。
image.english: Thunder on the mountain: Preponderance of the Small. The noble one, in conduct, exceeds in reverence; in mourning, exceeds in grief; in expenditure, exceeds in frugality. Exceeding — but only in the direction of care, not ambition.

judgment.chinese: 小過：亨，利貞。可小事，不可大事。飛鳥遺之音，不宜上宜下，大吉。
judgment.english: Preponderance of the Small. Success. Perseverance is favorable. Small things may be done; great things should not be done. The flying bird leaves behind its song — it is not fitting to strive upward, but fitting to remain below. Great good fortune. In this time, modesty exceeds and that is correct.

lines.chinese: 初六：飛鳥以凶。
lines.english: The bird flies up — misfortune. Rising when one should stay low. The time calls for restraint, not ascent.

lines.chinese: 六二：過其祖，遇其妣。不及其君，遇其臣，無咎。
lines.english: Passing by the grandfather, one meets the grandmother. Not reaching the prince, one meets the minister. No blame. One does not reach the highest, but finds what is appropriate at a lesser level. This is enough.

lines.chinese: 九三：弗過防之，從或戕之，凶。
lines.english: If one does not take extraordinary precautions, someone may come from behind and strike. Misfortune. In a time of small excess, ordinary caution is not enough.

lines.chinese: 九四：無咎，弗過遇之，往厲必戒，勿用永貞。
lines.english: No blame. Without exceeding, one meets the situation. Going forward is dangerous — one must be on guard. Do not use this as a permanent way. A temporary measure, not a principle.

lines.chinese: 六五：密雲不雨，自我西郊。公弋取彼在穴。
lines.english: Dense clouds, no rain, from the western outskirts. The duke shoots and takes the one in the cave. The conditions gather but do not yet release. Precision in small matters succeeds where large gestures would not.

lines.chinese: 上六：弗遇過之，飛鳥離之，凶，是謂災眚。
lines.english: Not meeting it but passing beyond it. The flying bird departs from it. Misfortune. This is called calamity and injury. Overshooting the mark entirely — what was small becomes catastrophic through excess.

image.chinese: 水在火上，既濟。君子以思患而豫防之。
image.english: Water over fire: After Completion. The noble one reflects on misfortune and arms against it in advance. The very completeness of the situation is what demands caution. What is perfectly balanced is most susceptible to disturbance.

judgment.chinese: 既濟：亨小，利貞。初吉終亂。
judgment.english: After Completion. Success in small matters. Perseverance is favorable. Good fortune at the beginning, disorder at the end. Everything is in its proper place — and that is precisely the danger. When the peak has been reached, decline begins. Vigilance, not celebration.

lines.chinese: 初九：曳其輪，濡其尾，無咎。
lines.english: Dragging one's wheels, getting one's tail wet. No blame. Holding back at the start, even when everything seems ready. Restraint at the moment of completion is wisdom.

lines.chinese: 六二：婦喪其茀，勿逐，七日得。
lines.english: The woman loses the curtain of her carriage. Do not pursue it. In seven days it will be recovered. What is lost in the transition will return on its own. Do not chase it.

lines.chinese: 九三：高宗伐鬼方，三年克之，小人勿用。
lines.english: The Illustrious Ancestor campaigns against the demon territory. After three years he conquers it. Inferior people should not be employed. Even after completion, difficult work remains. Undertake it with the right people — it will take longer than expected.

lines.chinese: 六四：繻有衣袽，終日戒。
lines.english: Fine silk garments — but underneath, rags for plugging leaks. Be on guard all day long. Beneath the appearance of completion, there are breaches. Attend to them constantly.

lines.chinese: 九五：東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之禴祭，實受其福。
lines.english: The eastern neighbor slaughters an ox, but the western neighbor's simple spring offering actually receives the blessing. Sincerity in small things surpasses lavishness. What matters is the inner attitude, not the scale of the gesture.

lines.chinese: 上六：濡其首，厲。
lines.english: Getting one's head wet. Danger. Going too far into the water after the crossing is complete. The completion has passed — continuing forward now means submersion.

image.chinese: 火在水上，未濟。君子以慎辨物居方。
image.english: Fire over water: Before Completion. The noble one is careful in discriminating among things, so that each finds its proper place. Nothing is settled yet. The work of sorting and placing continues.

judgment.chinese: 未濟：亨。小狐汔濟，濡其尾，無攸利。
judgment.english: Before Completion. Success. The small fox has almost crossed the stream, but gets its tail wet. Nothing is favorable. Nearly there — but the final step requires as much care as the first. Premature confidence is the danger. The transition is not yet complete.

lines.chinese: 初六：濡其尾，吝。
lines.english: Getting one's tail wet. Humiliation. Plunging forward without assessing depth. The beginning of an incomplete crossing — restraint would serve better than haste.

lines.chinese: 九二：曳其輪，貞吉。
lines.english: Dragging one's wheels. Perseverance brings good fortune. Holding back, not rushing toward completion. The braking force is what keeps things on course.

lines.chinese: 六三：未濟，征凶，利涉大川。
lines.english: Before completion. Advancing brings misfortune. It is favorable to cross the great water. A paradox: one cannot advance piecemeal, but one can commit fully. Half-measures fail; wholehearted effort succeeds.

lines.chinese: 九四：貞吉，悔亡。震用伐鬼方，三年有賞于大國。
lines.english: Perseverance brings good fortune. Remorse disappears. Shock — used to campaign against the demon territory. After three years, one is rewarded by the great nation. Sustained effort through difficulty. The reward comes, but not quickly.

lines.chinese: 六五：貞吉，無悔。君子之光，有孚，吉。
lines.english: Perseverance brings good fortune. No remorse. The light of the noble one. There is sincerity. Good fortune. Genuine radiance — not the light of completion, but the light of character that shines regardless of circumstance.

lines.chinese: 上九：有孚于飲酒，無咎。濡其首，有孚失是。
lines.english: Sincerity in drinking wine. No blame. But getting one's head wet — even with sincerity, one loses what is right. Celebration before the work is done. A little is acceptable; too much and the sincerity itself is drowned.
